objections.claim: Known array coercions preserve input collation through target.collationResult without modeling native ArrayCoerceExpr element collation. Consequently the independent rules and executable checker certify incorrect exact outputCollations, including database-default instead of C and POSIX instead of indeterminate. This is a successful native evaluation/metadata discrepancy, not literal conversion, cardinality, or locale comparison execution failure.

reproducer.sql: SELECT CAST((SELECT ARRAY['x']) AS NAME[]) AS v
reproducer.no_subquery_control: SELECT CAST(COALESCE(ARRAY['x']) AS NAME[]) AS v
reproducer.conflicting_input_sql: SELECT CAST((SELECT ARRAY['x'] COLLATE "POSIX") AS NAME[]) AS v
reproducer.polymorphic_operator_sql: SELECT ARRAY[(SELECT CAST('x' AS NAME) COLLATE "POSIX")] || ARRAY['x'] AS v
cli: SELECT CAST((SELECT ARRAY['x']) AS NAME[]) AS v
reproducer.native_observation: SELECT pg_typeof(v)::text, pg_typeof(v)::oid, pg_collation_for(v), pg_collation_for(v) IS NULL, v::text FROM (SELECT CAST((SELECT ARRAY['x']) AS NAME[]) AS v) q;

controls: CAST(ARRAY['x'] AS NAME[]) correctly reports/native-observes C because direct constructor targeting is separate.
CAST((SELECT 'x') AS NAME) correctly reports/native-observes default; applying an unconditional NAME-target C reset to scalar casts would regress this.
Array concat with direct explicit POSIX retains POSIX; wrapping that input inside scalar SELECT reduces strength to implicit and exposes the conflict.
NAME[] to TEXT[] with implicit POSIX remains POSIX; TEXT[] to NAME[] with implicit POSIX becomes indeterminate.
Native type OIDs: NAME 19/C=950, TEXT 25/default=100, NAME[] 1003/C=950, TEXT[] 1009/default=100; relevant array_cat operator OID375 uses anycompatiblearray.
